Reproducibility: yes. for source-level reproduction: current main and v0.34.0 still render root curl-to-shell installer paths for Code Server and package-mode Tailscale. I did not run a live upstream compromise, and the PR's own Tailscale managed-lease proof remains incomplete.

target.title: fix: harden managed Linux bootstrap
target.body:
Closes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/issues/715.

Supersedes https://github.com/openclaw/crabbox/pull/742 because GitHub rejected maintainer pushes to the contributor fork despite `maintainerCanModify=true`. The replacement preserves Andy Ye as co-author and keeps @TurboTheTurtle's changelog credit.

## Summary

- Replace managed Linux Code Server root installer scripts with pinned, checksum-verified archives in both CLI and coordinator bootstrap generators.
- Preserve Tailscale's existing default `package` contract through its signed APT repository with a checksum-pinned keyring; keep checksum-verified static archives as the explicit `pinned` mode.
- Keep Go and Worker mode parsing aligned, including case-insensitive `pinned` selection.
- Remove downloaded archives before copying install roots and disarm temporary-directory traps after successful cleanup.
- Update operator documentation and regression coverage.

## Verification

- `go test ./internal/cli` — pass.
- `npm test --prefix worker` — 25 files, 754 tests passed.
- `go vet ./...` — pass.
- Worker format, lint, typecheck, and dry-run build — pass.
- Docs command surface, provider matrix, links, and site build — pass.
- Focused Go and Worker bootstrap tests — pass after rebasing onto current `main`.
- Autoreview — clean after fixing a Go/Worker install-mode parity finding; replacement-branch autoreview also clean.
- Ephemeral Ubuntu 24.04 package canary — pinned keyring checksum verified, signed stable repository installed Tailscale 1.98.8, and package provenance resolved to `pkgs.tailscale.com`.

## Remaining live gate

Run one disposable managed Linux lease with Tailscale enabled, verify the client version and a `100.x` tailnet address, then prove provider key, VM, and tailnet-node cleanup. The one-off credential must remain private and be injected only for that validation run.
